claim: A child process is launched from an absolute program path and a list of argument values, so a shell metacharacter inside an argument arrives as literal text — never as a second command.

steps.label: ordinary arguments reach the child intact
steps.evidence: the child echoed its own argv back

steps.label: an argument full of shell metacharacters
steps.evidence: one argument, unsplit — nothing parsed it
steps.note: The check is not 'does this look dangerous'. It is 'is this ever interpreted', and the answer is no, by construction.

steps.label: a relative program name
steps.note: A bare name resolves through PATH, so it names a different file depending on where the process was started.

steps.label: the whole command line as one string
steps.detail: arguments must be a list of values, not one command line
steps.note: Something has to parse that back into a process, and that something is a shell.
